description: Manage this Organization's Agents, Skills and Projects as the human who created the calling Project.

connect_project.title: Connect to an environment
connect_project.description: Wakes the environment if it is asleep and answers once its opencode runtime is ready and the Project's primary Session is bound. The answer is everything a client needs to talk to the runtime directly: where it is, where its own OpenAPI document is, which Session to open and which build answered.

create_agent.title: Create a Custom Agent
create_agent.description: Creates an Agent private to you, with a kebab-case slug derived from `displayName` and a Development profile carrying an empty prompt, the given or default model pair, and the built-in `platform` Skill. The slug cannot change afterwards; a slug the deployment already uses is refused with 409.

displayName.description: The slug is derived from this and cannot change later

model.description: provider/model from the deployment catalog; defaults to the registry default

variant.description: Reasoning effort; must be one the model offers

create_project.title: Create a Project
create_project.description: Answers at once, normally with the Development environment still starting; poll the Project until it reports active. Omit workspaceId and the Project lands where the app would put it: a member gets their Personal workspace, a service account the tenant-wide Public area. A tenant with private workspaces turned off puts every omitted placement in Public.

agentId.description: Agent profile the Project runs, from GET /agents

workspaceId.description: Workspace to create the Project in; omit to use the default placement

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, defaults to UTC

kind.description: Only an Agent Caller running a Builder chat may send this, and only as "test": it makes the chat's one Test Project, which stays out of every Project list and lives as long as the chat. A second one answers 409 test-project-exists with its testProjectId; refresh that one with Update or Reset instead. It reads the Agent's Development, and an Agent chat may name only its own Agent

create_skill.title: Create a Skill
create_skill.description: Submits a whole file tree and, if it passes the validation gate, creates the Skill private to you at Version 1. There is no draft: saving is publishing. A tree that fails answers 422 with every error and lint, each carrying its rule, file and line, so a failed submission is a work list rather than a dead end.

name.description: Kebab-case, equal to the SKILL.md frontmatter name

files.description: The whole file tree, SKILL.md included; a submission replaces nothing, it mints a Version

create_skill_version.title: Publish a new Version
create_skill_version.description: Submits the whole tree again and mints the next integer Version, moving the Skill's latest pointer. Agents keep the Version they pinned and start showing "update available"; nothing upgrades on its own.

files.description: The whole file tree, SKILL.md included; a submission replaces nothing, it mints a Version

delete_project.title: Delete a Project
delete_project.description: Permanent, and requires can_delete_project. The Project, its environments and their pods are gone; a second call answers 404. A Project you cannot see answers 404 before the permission is even checked.

duplicate_skill.title: Duplicate a Skill
duplicate_skill.description: Copies the source's latest Version into a new private Skill of your own under a new name, rewriting the frontmatter `name` to match. Nothing about the source is recorded, and the copy never follows it.

name.description: Name of the new private Skill

get_agent.title: Get an Agent
get_agent.description: One Agent with its settings and one entry per Environment of the tenant. Every entry carries `environmentId`; `skills: null` marks an Environment this Agent has no profile at, which is how you tell "never published there" from "published with no Skills".

get_me.title: Get the current user
get_me.description: Who the token belongs to, where it can act, and what it may do. The id is the platform user id used everywhere else in this API, not the subject of your token. `tenants` lists every tenant you belong to; `tenant` is the one this call used. Permissions are the can_* names you hold, sorted.

get_project.title: Get a Project
get_project.description: One Project by id. A Project in another tenant, in a workspace you are not in, or that never existed all answer 404 alike, so the API never confirms a hidden Project is there.

get_skill.title: Get a Skill
get_skill.description: One Skill by id, with its latest Version, its flags and how many Agents carry it. A Skill you cannot see answers 404.

get_skill_files.title: Read the files of a Version
get_skill_files.description: Every file of one Version, `SKILL.md` first as it is stored. Text arrives as UTF-8 in `content`; a binary file arrives base64 with `isBinary` true.

list_agent_skills.title: List an Agent's Skills
list_agent_skills.description: The Skills the Agent's Development profile carries, each with the Version it pins and whether a newer one exists.

list_agents.title: List Agents
list_agents.description: The Agents you can build a Project on. Pass an id from here as agentId when creating one. Newest first; page with the opaque cursor.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the nextCursor of a previous page

list_projects.title: List Projects
list_projects.description: Every Project you can see in the selected tenant. Public Projects are visible to all members; a workspace Project only to that workspace. Disabled ones appear with disabled true. Newest first; page with the opaque cursor.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the nextCursor of a previous page

list_skills.title: List Skills
list_skills.description: Every Skill you can see: the Built-in ones the agent image ships, the public ones of your tenant, and your own private ones. Filter with `filter` and search with `q`; `filter=disabled` needs `can_manage_skills`.

filter.description: Defaults to all; disabled needs can_manage_skills

q.description: Substring match on name, display name and description

remove_agent_skill.title: Remove a Skill
remove_agent_skill.description: Takes the Skill off the Development profile. The Skill itself is untouched, and Projects already created keep their copy. The built-in `platform` Skill cannot be removed — every Agent inherits the platform's own harness through it.

reset_test_project.title: Reset a Test Project
reset_test_project.description: Stops the pod, wipes the workspace, and lays the Template, prompt and Skills from the Agent's Development exactly as a create does. It then unpins the primary Session, so the next Connect binds a new one, resets the Project's Bifrost spend, and starts the pod, so first boot runs again. The Project id, its side pane and its preview URL stay the same. Answers 204 once the pod is starting; poll Get a Project until environments[0].status is active, then Connect again.

restart_project.title: Restart a Project
restart_project.description: Throws the Development environment's pod away and starts a new one on the same workspace. Files under /workspace survive; everything installed into the container in chat does not, and startup.sh runs from cold — which is exactly what happens when a Project idles out or is published. Requires can_restart_project. Answers 204 at once; poll Get a Project until environments[0].status is active, then Connect again, because a new pod is a new Connection. A disabled Project answers 423.

save_agent_template.title: Save the Development Template
save_agent_template.description: Makes the Agent's Development Template an exact copy of the `template/` folder at the root of the calling Builder chat's workspace. There is no body: the folder is the input. A file deleted from `template/` leaves the Template, and a missing or empty `template/` removes it (`hash: null`). Saving the same files again gives the same `hash`. There is no size cap.

set_agent_skill.title: Add or re-pin a Skill
set_agent_skill.description: Puts the Skill on the Development profile, pinned to `versionId` or, with an empty object, to the latest Version. Sending it again with a newer `versionId` is the upgrade.

versionId.description: Pin this Version of the Skill; omit to pin the latest. Send {} to add at latest.

update_agent.title: Rename or describe an Agent
update_agent.description: Sets a Custom Agent's display name, or the one line the Store and the Project picker show under it. The slug stays what it was at creation, so Projects and links keep working.

displayName.description: The name people see; the slug never changes

description.description: One line on what the Agent is for; null clears it

update_agent_profile.title: Edit the Development profile
update_agent_profile.description: Overwrites the Development profile: prompt body, model and reasoning effort. There are no Agent versions — this is the working copy, and Projects created from it afterwards get it. Existing Projects keep the files they were created with.

promptBody.description: The whole system prompt body; it replaces the previous one

update_skill.title: Rename a Skill
update_skill.description: Sets the display name the Store and the Agent pages show. The `name` — the Skill's identity and its frontmatter `name` — stays what it was at creation.

displayName.description: The name people see; null falls back to `name`, which never changes

update_test_project.title: Update a Test Project
update_test_project.description: Overlays the Agent's saved Development Template onto the Test Project's workspace and commits the files it wrote as "Template update". It overwrites and adds, replacing a path the Template turned from a file into a folder or back, and deletes nothing else: remove a file the Template dropped through the shell yourself. The pod keeps running and the conversation carries on, so restart the Project yourself when something that runs has changed. The Project's Bifrost spend keeps its running total.

validate_skill.title: Validate a Skill tree
validate_skill.description: Runs the same gate a create or a new Version runs, and writes nothing. Answers 200 whether or not the tree passes: read `valid`, then `errors` and `lints`.

name.description: Check the frontmatter name against this one

files.description: The whole file tree, SKILL.md included; a submission replaces nothing, it mints a Version

path.description: Path relative to the Skill root; no leading slash and no ..

content.description: UTF-8 text, or base64 when isBinary is true
